papers.title: Aplicación del Small Punch Test en la caracterización mecánica de Ti-6Al-4V obtenido por fabricación aditiva
papers.abstract: mecánicamente estos materiales sigue siendo un reto por su anisotropía, heterogeneidad y defectos. El ensayo Small Punch Test (SPT) ofrece una solución eficaz cuando el material disponible es limitado, como en componentes biomédicos o de alto valor. Este estudio evalúa la aplicabilidad del SPT en la aleación Ti-6Al-4V fabricada por fusión por haz de electrones (EBM). Se validó la estimación de la resistencia máxima a la tracción (Rm) a partir de la carga máxima (Fm), normalizada por el espesor y el desplazamiento. En titanio forjado, los resultados mostraron buena correlación con ensayos tradicionales. En cambio, en muestras EBM se detectó mayor dispersión debido a anisotropía y defectos superficiales. Aun así, el SPT se consolida como una herramienta útil para el control de calidad con bajo consumo de material. Este trabajo sienta las bases para futuras investigaciones dirigidas a establecer correlaciones más robustas para materiales EBM y a comprender en profundidad la influencia de las orientaciones de construcción en sus propiedades mecánicas.

llm.why_not_core: does not provide standard tensile or fatigue data; focuses on method validation rather than comprehensive mechanical characterization

summary_zh.motivation: 为克服增材制造Ti-6Al-4V力学表征的样品限制，探索小冲杆测试的适用性。
summary_zh.method: 通过小冲杆测试获得载荷-位移数据，并建立与拉伸强度的关联模型。
summary_zh.result: 小冲杆测试能有效估计强度，但EBM样品因缺陷和各向异性导致分散性较大。
summary_zh.validation: 与锻造Ti-6Al-4V的传统拉伸试验进行对比验证。

summary_en.motivation: The study investigates the applicability of the Small Punch Test for mechanical characterization of additively manufactured Ti-6Al-4V when material is limited.
summary_en.method: Small Punch Test was performed on EBM Ti-6Al-4V specimens, and correlations between maximum load and ultimate tensile strength were established with normalization by thickness and displacement.
summary_en.result: SPT showed good correlation for wrought Ti-6Al-4V but higher scatter for EBM specimens due to anisotropy and surface defects.
summary_en.validation: Validation was conducted by comparing SPT-derived strength estimates with conventional tensile test results for wrought Ti-6Al-4V.

papers.title: Effect of Thermal Oxidation Parameters on Morphological Properties of Thermal Oxide Coatings on Ti6Al4V Titanium Alloy
papers.abstract: The effects of thermal oxidation temperature and treatment route on the morphology of oxide coatings formed on Ti6Al4V alloy were systematically investigated. Ti6Al4V samples were subjected to different oxidation treatments, namely annealing, normalizing, and air-quenching—at temperatures of 850 and 900 ℃. The surface morphology and compositional features of the resulting oxide coatings were characterized. In addition, the coating thickness and weight gain per unit area (ΔW/A) were quantitatively evaluated. The results indicate that nearly all oxidation treatments produced continuous, well-adhered, and largely defect-free oxide coatings on the Ti6Al4V substrate. Annealing at both temperatures led to the formation of uniform and dense oxide layers predominantly composed of TiO₂ (rutile phase). In contrast, normalizing resulted in comparatively thinner oxide coatings exhibiting minor surface scars and increased roughness, while air-quenched specimens developed thicker oxide layers accompanied by slight surface spallation and micro-crack formation at both temperatures. The oxide coating formed by annealing at 900 ℃ exhibited a moderate thickness of 195 ± 9.75 µm. Moreover, annealing at 900 ℃ yielded the highest ΔW/A of 126 ± 6.3 mg/cm². Overall, among the investigated treatments, annealing at 900 ℃ produced oxide coatings with the most favorable morphological characteristics.

papers.title: Influence of laser surface remelting process on the mechanical properties of Ti6Al4V samples produced by selective laser melting
papers.abstract: O controle da rugosidade superficial é um aspecto crítico na fabricação de componentes de Ti6Al4V produzidos por fusão a laser em leito de pó (L-PBF). As superfícies resultantes exibiram alta rugosidade, exigindo pós-processamento para aplicações específicas. A fusão a laser (LSM) surgiu como um processo promissor. A rugosidade superficial influencia diretamente o comportamento mecânico de um componente. Assim, o controle do acabamento superficial garante maior confiabilidade estrutural em serviço, permitindo inspeções programadas. O processo LSM foi realizado usando um laser de Yb:fibra com potência de 130 W, velocidade de varredura de 50 mm/s, espaçamento de trilhas de 0,1 mm e argônio como gás de processo (9 l/min). Análises de rugosidade e difração de raios X foram usadas para identificar as fases formadas e avaliar os níveis de tensão residual. A rugosidade superficial (Ra) foi reduzida em 56% por meio desse processo. A análise de difração de raios X revelou uma microestrutura composta pela fase α-Ti; No entanto, o processo LSM induziu uma textura superficial e promoveu um aumento de 44% no tamanho dos grãos devido à coalescência dos grãos durante a refusão. A análise de tensões residuais revelou que a superfície original estava livre de tensões, enquanto após o LSM, apresentou tensões compressivas. Portanto, o processo LSM é eficaz no controle da rugosidade, não causa alterações microestruturais e induz tensões compressivas na superfície, o que é benéfico para o comportamento mecânico.

llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on laser surface remelting (LSM) post-processing of Ti6Al4V and reports only surface roughness, XRD, and residual stress; it provides no mechanical testing (tensile, fatigue, hardness) and thus does not contribute to the base mechanical/fatigue characterization required by Layer 1.

summary_zh.motivation: 控制SLM Ti6Al4V的表面粗糙度以提高机械可靠性。
summary_zh.method: 采用Yb:光纤激光对Ti6Al4V进行表面重熔处理。
summary_zh.result: 表面粗糙度降低56%，残余应力变为压应力，晶粒尺寸增加44%。
summary_zh.validation: 通过粗糙度测量、XRD和残余应力分析进行表征。

summary_en.motivation: To control the surface roughness of SLM-produced Ti6Al4V components, which is critical for mechanical reliability.
summary_en.method: Laser surface remelting (LSM) was applied using a Yb:fiber laser at 130 W, 50 mm/s scan speed, 0.1 mm hatch spacing, and argon shielding.
summary_en.result: Surface roughness (Ra) was reduced by 56%, compressive residual stresses were induced, and grain size increased by 44% due to coalescence during remelting.
summary_en.validation: Surface roughness measurements, X-ray diffraction for phase identification and texture, and residual stress analysis were conducted.

papers.title: Comparison of ultrasonic surface treatment methods applied to additively manufactured Ti-6Al-4V alloy
papers.abstract: Introduction. Selective Laser Melting (SLM) of metal powders enables the fabrication of parts with arbitrary geometries, which is unattainable through conventional manufacturing technologies. The main disadvantages of the method include high surface roughness, resulting from metal spattering, spheroidization, partial melting and powder adhesion, as well as difficulties with finishing complex surface areas. One effective approach for processing such parts is the application of ultrasonic liquid technologies, where cavitation bubbles act as working bodies, penetrating and performing work on any area of the surface. The purpose of this study is to determine the influence of different types of ultrasonic treatment on the surface properties obtained by selective laser melting through comparative testing. Materials and methods. Samples made from Ti-6Al-4V titanium alloy, manufactured using selective laser melting on an EOS M280 machine, were investigated. For ultrasonic treatment, a rod-shaped magnetostrictive vibratory system was used, with the end of the emitter positioned 20 mm from the side surface of the sample. A etching solution (3% HF + 5% HNO3 + H2O) was used as a liquid medium to remove the oxide film that hinders the effect of cavitation. Cavitation-erosion (CET) treatment, cavitation-abrasive (CAT) treatment, and additionally, ultrasonic surface plastic deformation (USPD) were performed. After treatment, the surface condition, roughness, and sub-microgeometry were assessed for all samples. The microstructure of the USPD-treated samples was also investigated. Results and discussion. A high-speed imaging method was used to compare the main mechanisms of interaction with the surface during CET and CAT. During CET, collapsing and pulsating cavitation clusters are observed, located at the points of highest peaks and valleys on the surface. During CAT, the micro-cutting action of abrasive particles is added. These particles receive shock waves generated by collapsing bubbles, hit the surface, and undergo oscillatory, rotational, and longitudinal movements. Comparison of the surface condition dynamics revealed that CET enables complete removal of surface defects down to the melt tracks. CAT removes some surface defects while deforming the remaining ones. During USPD, spherical defects are crushed, forming large flat areas. All types of ultrasonic treatment reduce surface roughness: Ra is reduced by 33% during CET, by 43% during CAT, and by 52% during USPD. However, Rmax is lowest with CAT. The microstructure after USPD is characterized by a hardened layer with a depth of approximately 100 µm and an increase in microhardness up to 35%. However, after USPD, defects in the form of cracks, partially deformed spheres, and the presence of untreated deep surface depressions are formed in the surface layer, which significantly reduces performance characteristics. Therefore, it is advisable to perform CET or CAT before USPD to remove surface defects.

papers.title: Thermo mechanical Finite Element Analysis of the plasma Wire Arc Additive Manufacturing process in DEFORM® 13
papers.abstract: This study investigates the potential of Finite Element Analysis in DEFORM® to predict the thermal history, deformation, residual stress state and grain growth in the Wire Arc Additive Manufacturing processes of Ti-6Al-4V. The temperature dependent material model for Ti-6Al-4V was extended and adapted to improve the representation of contact boundary conditions within DEFORM®, focusing on Additive Manufacturing. A single layer quad-mesh approach was employed alongside dummy heat sources to simulate the process by accurate layer wise activation within the arc welding module. The model utilized a normalized double-ellipsoid heat source and introduced a power adaptation strategy to account for differences in volumetric deposition. The extracted thermal history showed very good agreement to corresponding thermocouple measurements. The accuracy of the resulting deformation state was validated using a 3D scan, while the predicted grain size distribution was compared against an as-built micrograph. The simulation showed good overall accuracy, though limitations were noted in the grain size model, which was inadequate in predicting the more complex texture of the mixed α / β -microstructure typical for Ti-6Al-4V. Seven heat treatment strategies were evaluated to address mechanical anisotropy. Solution annealing followed by water quenching and subsequent low temperature aging was found to be most effective. • Thermo-Mechanical Finite Element Model of Wire Arc Additive Manufacturing in DEFORM®. • Independent element activation for a volumetric heat source model in arc welding. • Optimized boundary conditions for Ti-6Al-4V in Additive Manufacturing.

llm.why_not_core: No experimental fatigue or tensile data; the study focuses on process simulation and grain size prediction, not quantitative mechanical performance after post-processing.

summary_zh.motivation: 通过有限元模拟预测线弧增材制造Ti-6Al-4V的热历程和变，并评估热处理对力学各向异性的影响。
summary_zh.method: 在DEFORM中建立热-力-微观组织耦合模型，采用双椭球热源和逐层激活，对比七种热处理工艺。
summary_zh.result: 模拟与实验吻合良好，固溶+水淬+时效热处理最有效降低各向异性。
summary_zh.validation: 热电偶验证热历程，3D扫描验证变形，金相验证晶粒尺寸。

summary_en.motivation: This study aims to simulate the thermal history, deformation, and residual stress of wire arc additive manufacturing of Ti-6Al-4V and to evaluate post-processing heat treatments to mitigate mechanical anisotropy.
summary_en.method: A thermo-mechanical finite element model was developed in DEFORM® using a normalized double-ellipsoid heat source and element activation, and seven heat treatment strategies were compared.
summary_en.result: The simulation predictions agreed well with experimental measurements, and solution annealing followed by water quenching and low-temperature aging was identified as the most effective treatment for reducing anisotropy.
summary_en.validation: The model was validated against thermocouple measurements for thermal history, a 3D scan for deformation, and an as-built micrograph for grain size distribution.

papers.title: Development of Two-Color Pyrometer for Film Cooling and Transpiration Cooling at High Temperature Conditions
papers.abstract: Abstract This study used a non-invasive two-color pyrometry to investigate transpiration cooling and film cooling on a flat-plate model. Unlike typical infrared thermography, this technique is not affected by changes in emissivity due to heating. An industrial camera captured light intensity through interference filters of different wavelengths (1250 nm and 1550 nm) to calculate the target surface’s temperature and emissivity. Calibration was done using a blackbody furnace with temperatures ranging from 375°C to 600 °C. The test was performed in a high-temperature wind tunnel capable of reaching a mainstream flow temperature above 900°C, with test specimens measuring 60mm × 65mm × 4.5mm for film cooling and transpiration cooling. These samples were additively manufactured using Ti-6Al-4V, AISI-316L, and Inconel-718 materials. For film cooling, a fan-shaped hole configuration with a hole pitch-to-diameter ratio of 8 was applied, while for transpiration cooling, an Orthotropic Porous structure with a pore length of 0.4 mm was used. Results showed that the two-color pyrometry successfully measured surface temperature on different materials with less than 5% uncertainty in temperature measurement accuracy.

summary_en.motivation: To develop a non-invasive temperature measurement technique that is independent of surface emissivity for high-temperature cooling studies.
summary_en.method: A two-color pyrometer using an industrial camera with interference filters at 1250 nm and 1550 nm, calibrated with a blackbody furnace, was applied to measure surface temperature on film-cooled and transpiration-cooled flat plates.
summary_en.result: The technique successfully measured surface temperatures on Ti-6Al-4V and other additively manufactured specimens with an uncertainty below 5%.
summary_en.validation: Experimental validation was conducted in a high-temperature wind tunnel (mainstream >900°C) with blackbody calibration.
